newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to tell Clinton no budging on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to tell Clinton no budging on Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ceded nothing to Palestinians on Wednesday ahead of a White House peace-saving meeting in five days with U.S. President Bill Clinton.

Asked if Israel had anything to offer the Palestinian leadership in return for stopping attacks on Israelis, spokesman Shai Bazak said: "First of all and as a first condition, the cessation of Palestinian terrorism -- and only then the continuation of diplomatic negotiations."

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright called Palestinian President Yasser Arafat twice on Wednesday to hear his views on the situation ahead of Netanyahu's visit, the Palestinian news agency Wafa said.

The agency quoted Arafat as telling Albright: "The Israeli settlement policy...places the entire peace process in real danger." He said later only a halt in settlement building would calm the situation.
Palestinians complain Jewish settlement construction pre-empts the results of final peace talks yet to come on the status of East Jerusalem, which each side claims as its own.

But Netanyahu's media adviser, Bazak, told Israel's army radio the prime minister would tell Clinton that Israel was unyielding in its resolve to build the Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem that has sparked two weeks of clashes.
Palestinian stone-throwers on Wednesday clashed north of Jersualem with soldiers who responded with teargas and rubber bullets.
A bus carrying Israeli troops overturned in the West Bank, injuring three soldiers, after Palestinians threw a petrol bomb at the vehicle, Jewish settlers said.
Palestinian security officials confirmed a bus with soldiers had overturned near Jalazoun refugee camp, north of Jerusalem, but gave no details. The Israeli army said it was checking the report.

"The building at Har Homa will continue," Bazak said. "He (Netanyahu) will say that to Clinton. He has said that to the whole world and he will say it again. Jerusalem is the capital of Israel and we have the right to build in it."
An opinion poll of 509 Israeli Jews published in the newspaper Maariv showed 52 percent backed continuing construction of the settlement.
Bazak said the Israeli leader would arrive in Washington on Monday morning and return home the same night.

"We go to Washington with a clear desire of ours and I think the Americans to clarify to the Palestinians that if terrorism continues it will be hard to continue the peace process at the same time," Bazak said.
Clinton, involved in Israeli-PLO deals since the first was signed at the White House in 1993, pledged to get personally involved again on Tuesday when he met Jordan's King Hussein in Washington.
"I'm prepared personally to do anything I can to get this process back on track and move it forward," Clinton said.
In the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip on Tuesday, two Palestinians were killed in explosions that Israel said were botched suicide bombings by the Islamic Jihad group aimed at Jewish school children.

Jihad sources said on Wednesday the Palestinian Authority had arrested 30 of their activists in overnight raids. But the group disavowed the two bombings, charging instead that Israel had staged them to divert attention from its settlement policy.

"The Islamic Jihad movement in Palestine denies any responsibility for the two suspected explosions yesterday and has no link at all to them," Islamic Jihad leader in Gaza Sheikh Abdallah al-Shami said.
Some 1,500 Palestinian protesters marched in the West Bank town of Nablus a day after a Palestinian policeman was killed in a clash with Israeli troops. The march ended peacefully.
